analysis.summary: The PR migrates to SST and AWS endpoints but introduces a critical authentication mismatch between the client and BFF, along with incorrect analytics data structures for new tracking events.

bugs.title: BFF Authentication Failure due to Missing API Key Headers
bugs.description: The BFF handlers are now configured to require an 'x-api-key' header (via staticVerifySecret), but the client-side fetch calls in post-form-to-endpoint.ts and fetch-app-model.ts were updated to remove the previous secret-sending logic without adding the new header.
bugs.risk: All requests from the Feature App to the BFF (app-model and post-form) will fail with 401/403 errors, rendering the forms non-functional in production.

bugs.title: Incorrect Analytics Data Structure for Page View Events
bugs.description: New analytics events like 'pcp-confirmation-page' use a 'page' property structure, but are passed to provideAnalytics with a type assertion (as ISmartEvt17 | ISmartEvt14) that requires an 'eventInfo' property.
bugs.risk: The analytics provider will fail to find the expected 'eventInfo' object for page views, leading to either silent tracking failures or runtime errors when attempting to access properties of undefined.

bugs.title: BFF Configuration Uses Undefined unsubscriptionConfiguration
bugs.description: The bff handler attempts to use 'unsubscriptionConfiguration' when the view is 'unsubscription', but this variable is not defined or imported within the scope of the file after the refactor.
bugs.risk: Submitting an unsubscription request will trigger a ReferenceError, causing the Lambda function to crash and the unsubscription feature to fail.
bugs.codeSnippet:
const transformed = await transformer(
      view !== `unsubscription` ? null : unsubscriptionConfiguration,
      payload,
      sessionToken,

notBugs.reason: Passing null as the configuration parameter to transformers is safe because the new fetchAWSApiEndpoint implementation derives the base URL from the envName parameter rather than the configuration object.
Passing marketId and campaignId as extra trailing arguments to transformer functions is safe as JavaScript naturally ignores additional arguments not specified in the function signature.
